hero.tagline: From theory to industry disruption — understand what smart contracts can and cannot do for your business.

section1.title: Introduction to Smart Contracts
section1.description: What smart contracts are in business terms, Nick Szabo's vending machine, the history — and an honest hype-vs-value check.

section2.title: How Smart Contracts Work
section2.description: What happens when a contract runs — Web3 stack, dApps, token standards and gas — told for decision-makers, with the code kept optional.

section3.title: Industries & Case Studies
section3.description: Five industry verticals, a deep block on NFT utility and DAO governance structures, and six flagship cases including Walmart, Santander, the CA DMV and the TradeLens shutdown.

section4.title: Critical Thinking
section4.description: Decision framework: when to use a smart contract — and when not to. Plus the 5-pillar adoption model for serious business deployment.

section5.title: Limitations & Risks
section5.description: Oracle problem, blockchain trilemma, security risks, a gallery of six real failures (Ronin, Beanstalk, Terra…), cost realities and regulatory uncertainty.

section6.title: Build & Integration
section6.description: Optional, developer-oriented: ERC standards, EIP process, frameworks, platform comparison and integration patterns. Skipped in lecture.

section7.title: In-class Assignment
section7.description: In small groups: pick a real-world problem, discuss it, and submit a one-page report — problem, proposed solution, and the pros & cons of using a blockchain.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.description: Smart contracts are not magic — they are code. Their power and their risk come from the same source.
